extractedText: Base44 launches in-house LLM to help users build apps with natural language Tuesday, 30 June 2026, 06:06 Base44 has started training its own model to cut inference costs and control data, aiming to strengthen platform defensibility against frontier AI rivals. As noted by Techcrunch Base44 is a vibe-coding platform that Wix acquired for $80 million a year ago, when the company had existed for only six months and had a team of eight people. Today it has begun deploying its own AI model designed to help users build applications using natural language. The movement is set against increasingly active discussions in the AI field about whether it makes sense to rely on frontier models or to develop own solutions for long-term defensibility of products. The Base44 company, based near San Francisco, places this question at the forefront. Training and owning the model as part of the entire stack allow us to significantly optimize latency, cost, and efficiency. – Maor Shlomo Defensibility and Competition At first glance, the initiative could give Base44 an edge over competitors, including the Swedish startup Lovable, which rose to unicorn status after a Series A round last summer and is directing its development toward external LLMs. However, Maor Shlomo believes that other players can also train their own models – at least those who have reached scale and speed to collect enough data. According to Jonathan Userovici, General Partner at Headline – a venture fund whose portfolio includes AI platforms such as Mistral AI – data remains one of the three key components of defensibility for AI startups, alongside distribution and the tech stack. Base44, however, is not in Headline’s portfolio. The outlook points to a trend: branded players are increasingly investing in data and infrastructure to boost defensibility. Base44 is responding to the trend: the first version of their LLM – Base1 – was trained on a dataset formed from tens of millions of real user interactions on the platform. This dataset will undoubtedly grow with the company, but competitors will not stay idle. Significant competition may come not only from vibe-code startups, but also from frontier AI laboratories approaching Base44’s domain: Cursor and Grok – the parent company of which, xAI, is now owned by SpaceX; Claude Code has also emerged on the scene. This opens access for Anthropic and other foundational AI providers to data and feedback that can be used to improve models for building applications. Shlomo believes that specializing in particular niches gives Base44 an edge over competitors. Models are advancing, but they will remain very general in what they can do. – Maor Shlomo According to Jonathan Userovici, one should not underestimate the role of frontier models: Harvey – a legal startup that rejected plans to train its own model – is a case in point. He doesn’t expect applied AI to become a mass frontier-lab, but he believes that Base44’s approach aligns with the broader context – inference costs are becoming a key factor in business decisions. According to him, cost pressure is already forcing client teams to seek orchestration and optimization: selecting the right models for specific scenarios and controlling costs without sacrificing the required performance under different usage conditions. Although Base44’s reach is not yet widespread, the company continues to grow after the Wix acquisition: Wix reported ARR above $100 million. At the same time, Lovable demonstrates significant ARR, around half a billion dollars, signaling high competitive intensity in the market. Maor Shlomo believes that “significant engineering efforts” in developing Base1 will help Base44 establish itself as the “single vertically integrated vibe-coding platform” – that is, a player who controls distribution, data, and infrastructure simultaneously. In summary, Base44 aims to strengthen its position by building its own model and achieving full vertical integration, with a focus on reducing costs and increasing productivity for business clients. Such an approach could reinforce the platform’s defensibility in a competitive market where data, distribution, and infrastructure come to the forefront. Don’t miss other news: European startup Lovable exceeded $500 million ARR and now generates about one million new projects per week, demonstrating rapid vibe coding adoption while raising questions about long term maintainability.
